To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the development of the radiolabeled exendin-based imaging and radiotheranostic agents targeting GLP-1R is an emerging area in diabetes and oncologic imaging and radiotherapy; 2) the radiolabeled GLP-1 analogs are a promising tool for imaging and radiotherapy of GLP-1 receptors in diabetes, neuroendocrine tumors and small cell lung cancer; 3) the GLP-1-based radiolabeled agents are promising tools
radiolabeled exendin-based GLP-1 analogs can be used for imaging and therapy of GLP-1 receptors.
the radiolabeled GLP-1-based agents targeting GLP-1R can be used as imaging and radiotherapeutics in oncology and diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new radiolabeled imaging agents for the detection of tumors and the development of new radiotherapeutic agents for the treatment of tumors.
development of radiolabeling methods and evaluation of radiotracer properties of GLP-1R-targeted radiopharmaceuticals for diagnosis and therapy of diabetes and oncology.
the design of radiolabeled agents for the imaging of GLP-1R and the radiotherapeutic applications of such agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of radiometal labeled exendin-3, -4 and -11 analogs is in its early stages.
the development of GLP-1 radiolabeled agents has reached a mature stage and is moving toward a clinical application in the field of personalized medicine.
exendin-4-based imaging agents have been developed and evaluated in preclinical and clinical studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of radiopharmaceuticals for GLP-1R imaging is in its infancy.
the radiolabeled exendin-based GLP-1R agonists are promising candidates for both imaging and therapy of diabetes and cancers.
radiolabeled exendin-4 and its derivatives have been successfully developed for imaging and therapy in diabetes and oncologic applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of imaging and radiotheranostic GLP-1 analogs is a challenging task.
the development of exendin-based radiolabeled agents is a promising approach for personalized medicine in diabetes, oncology, and other diseases.
the radiolabeled exendin-based GLP-1R targeting agents can be used for both imaging and therapy.
